books.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.blurb: The twelve stories that put Baker Street on the map. A king who needs a photograph back, a pawnbroker paid to copy out the encyclopaedia, a speckled band and a whistle in the night at Stoke Moran. Our edition follows the 1892 Harper printing and keeps Sidney Paget's drawings, with a colour plate opening each story. Proofing copy: corrections welcome.
books.source: Harper & Brothers, New York, 1892 — collated from two scans of two copies of that printing, read independently
books.license: Text and Sidney Paget’s plates public domain; cover, Adventure plates and editorial matter © RFRMD Word Labs LLC

books.title: The Pilgrim's Progress
books.author: John Bunyan
books.blurb: The most widely read allegory in English, and still the best companion for the road. Christian sets out from the City of Destruction with a burden on his back, and the way to the Celestial City runs through the Slough of Despond, Vanity Fair and Doubting Castle. In Part Two his wife Christiana and their children follow after him. A book for every age in the house.
books.source: The Works of John Bunyan, ed. George Offor, 1855, via Project Gutenberg and Standard Ebooks
books.license: Text public domain; editorial matter © RFRMD Word Labs LLC, CC BY 4.0; cover and marks reserved

books.title: The Mortification of Sin in Believers
books.author: John Owen
books.blurb: Short, sharp and searching. Owen preached these sermons to Oxford students in 1656 on a single verse, Romans 8:13, and they remain the book many readers are handed first when a sin will not let go. He is just as clear on the ways we fool ourselves that the fight is over. From the 1668 printing. Proofing copy: corrections welcome.
books.source: EEBO-TCP A53715 (Wing O787), the 1668 printing, keyed and released CC0
books.license: Text public domain; editorial matter © RFRMD Word Labs LLC

books.title: The Rare Jewel of Christian Contentment
books.author: Jeremiah Burroughs
books.blurb: Contentment, Burroughs says, is learned, which means it can be taught. In these sermons on Philippians 4:11 he shows what true contentment is and is not, and answers one by one the excuses a restless heart makes. A Puritan classic that reads as if it were written this week. From the 1649 printing. Proofing copy: corrections welcome.
books.source: EEBO-TCP A30598 (Wing B6103), the 1649 printing, keyed and released CC0
books.license: Text public domain; editorial matter © RFRMD Word Labs LLC

books.title: Meditations and Discourses on the Glory of Christ
books.author: John Owen
books.blurb: Owen's last work, and two books in one. The Meditations dwell on the glory of Christ in his person, his office and his grace; the Discourses that complete them turn that glory toward the unbeliever and toward the Christian whose love has grown cold. Read together, each makes the other richer. Spelling is modernised; Scripture stands as printed. Proofing copy: corrections welcome.

books.title: The Sovereignty of God
books.author: A. W. Pink
books.blurb: Plain words on a hard subject. Pink sets out what Scripture says of God's rule over creation, salvation and the human will, then takes the usual objections one at a time. This is the full 1918 first edition, with the three appendices that later abridgements cut. Proofing copy: corrections welcome.

books.title: Treasure Island
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.blurb: The pirate story all the others borrow from. A dying sailor at the Admiral Benbow, a map in his sea-chest, and young Jim Hawkins bound for the island aboard the Hispaniola, alongside a ship's cook named Long John Silver who is far better company than he ought to be. Wonderful read aloud.

books.title: The Swiss Family Robinson
books.author: Johann David Wyss
books.blurb: Shipwrecked with each other and whatever they can save from the wreck, a father, a mother and four boys make a home on an unknown island, treehouse and all. Inventive, hopeful and full of practical wonder, and a family read-aloud for generations.

books.title: The Mystery at Dark Cedars
books.author: Edith Lavell
books.blurb: Meet Mary Louise Gay, sixteen and set on being a detective. Money is vanishing from a miserly old woman's shuttered house, and the orphaned niece takes the blame. Mary Louise is sure they have the wrong girl. A good old-fashioned mystery for young readers.
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: The Mystery of the Fires
books.author: Edith Lavell
books.blurb: A month at Shady Nook with her friend Jane, and Mary Louise means to do nothing but swim and canoe. Then a bungalow burns, then another, and the summer neighbours begin eyeing one another. She is on holiday. The fires are not.
books.source: Project Gutenberg ebook 43583, retrieved via OpenChapter.io
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: The Mystery of the Secret Band
books.author: Edith Lavell
books.blurb: Christmas is coming, and Mary Louise has her first real case: two weeks away from home, working at her father's trade at last. Then come the robberies. A midnight visitor, an empty house, a blow in the dark, and a gang nobody can name.
books.source: Project Gutenberg ebook 43584, retrieved via OpenChapter.io
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: Shenanigans at Sugar Creek
books.author: Paul Hutchens
books.blurb: A stern new teacher, a bald snowman made to mock him, and a board wired over the schoolhouse chimney. The gang gets the blame, and learns what kindness can do.
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: The Sugar Creek Gang Goes North
books.author: Paul Hutchens
books.blurb: Bill Collins and the gang head north to camp, hoping to see their friend Snow-in-the-face again. Instead they walk into a kidnapping. Boyhood adventure with a warm heart and a plain faith, the way the Sugar Creek books always are.
books.source: Project Gutenberg ebook 56554, retrieved via OpenChapter.io
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: The Sugar Creek Gang Digs for Treasure
books.author: Paul Hutchens
books.blurb: Little Jim and Bill play Robinson Crusoe on the lakeshore and dig for make-believe treasure, until the game turns real: a kidnapper, a ransom, and money nobody can find.
books.source: Project Gutenberg ebook 56553, retrieved via OpenChapter.io
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: North Woods Manhunt
books.author: Paul Hutchens
books.blurb: The ransom money is dug up, but John Till gets away from the old icehouse. A note in the night, a race to the Indian cemetery, and a cry for help on a moonlit lake finish the story begun in Digs for Treasure.
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: The Green Tent Mystery at Sugar Creek
books.author: Paul Hutchens
books.blurb: Walking home past the old cemetery on the darkest night of summer, three boys see a light among the gravestones and somebody digging. Just scary enough, and it keeps the Sugar Creek Gang busy until autumn.
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: Watermelon Mystery at Sugar Creek
books.author: Paul Hutchens
books.blurb: Bill's prize melon vanishes in the night, girl scouts take him for a zebra, and the woman in the green tent across the creek is not what she seems.
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

note: Every edition begins with a work long out of copyright, usually an original printing we can name. We set the text properly — collating the copies that survive, and clearing away what scanning and re-keying leave behind — so the book reads well on the page and sounds right read aloud. Where we mark a division inside a chapter, it is one the author announces himself. Every edition says on its own front matter what was done to its text. They are free to read and free to keep; our hope is that they reach people, grow their love for the Lord, and increase their joy in reading.
